summary_of_change:
In Q2 2026, Klarna delivered an earnings paradox: revenue grew 27% YoY to $1.042 billion and transaction margin dollars surged 42% YoY to $446 million, lifting GAAP net income into positive territory at $9 million ($0.01 per share). Active consumers reached 120 million, merchant partners expanded to over 1.2 million, and Q2 GMV climbed 18% YoY to $36.6 billion. 

Unit economics are visibly benefiting from a mix shift toward higher-yielding products, with ARPAC up 24% YoY to $33.7, 2 million paying membership subscribers, and 6.5 million active Klarna Card users. Credit provisions ticked down to 0.52% of GMV, while customer deposits scaled to $11.7 billion, funding 88% of the credit book and supporting a net balance sheet cash position of $+2,163M ($+3.64 per share).

2. 3-Year Unit Volume Extrapolation: Driven by international scaling of the Klarna Card and membership subscriptions, active consumers expand at a moderate CAGR to 155 million by Year 3, while ARPAC rises to $40.0 as users adopt broader digital banking services.

3. Projected Year 3 Revenue: Multiplying 155 million active consumers by an ARPAC of $40.0 yields a Projected Year 3 Revenue of $6,200.0M.

full_html_content:
What the Market is Pricing In

Mr. Market is currently pricing in a severe structural deceleration and terminal decay of Klarna's business model following its September 2025 IPO at $40. At the current market price of $14.29, investors have reacted aggressively to a lowered full-year GMV outlook caused by softness in core European markets like Germany, alongside the abrupt news of C-suite departures including the CFO and CMO for early 2027. The prevailing consensus view treats buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) as a low-barrier-to-entry, commoditized transaction pipe devoid of durable pricing power or customer loyalty.

Why the Market Might Be Right

Skeptics argue that despite recent GAAP profitability, Klarna remains exposed to cyclical credit shocks and severe margin compression if merchant take-rates erode under intense competition from legacy card networks and alternative digital wallets. Furthermore, execution risk is heavily magnified by leadership turnover in critical financial roles during a sensitive operational transition. If consumer defaults spike above historical bands or macroeconomic headwinds widen across European retail, the company's thin operating buffers leave little room for error on its $10.7 billion loan book.

How Things Are Going Now

In Q2 2026, Klarna delivered an earnings paradox: revenue grew 27% YoY to $1.042 billion and transaction margin dollars surged 42% YoY to $446 million, lifting GAAP net income into positive territory at $9 million ($0.01 per share). Active consumers reached 120 million, merchant partners expanded to over 1.2 million, and Q2 GMV climbed 18% YoY to $36.6 billion.

Unit economics are visibly benefiting from a mix shift toward higher-yielding products, with ARPAC up 24% YoY to $33.7, 2 million paying membership subscribers, and 6.5 million active Klarna Card users. Credit provisions ticked down to 0.52% of GMV, while customer deposits scaled to $11.7 billion, funding 88% of the credit book and supporting a net balance sheet cash position of \(+2,163M (\)+3.64 per share).

What If It Keeps Going That Way

Starting Unit Baseline

1
3-Year Unit Volume Extrapolation
Driven by international scaling of the Klarna Card and membership subscriptions, active consumers expand at a moderate CAGR to 155 million by Year 3, while ARPAC rises to $40.0 as users adopt broader digital banking services.
1
Projected Year 3 Revenue
Multiplying 155 million active consumers by an ARPAC of $40.0 yields a Projected Year 3 Revenue of $6,200.0M.
1
Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings
Applying an improved owner cash margin of 10.5% due to AI-driven operating leverage and lower deposit funding costs yields a Projected Year 3 Total Owner Earnings of $654.4M ($1.10 per share on 594.9M diluted shares).
1
Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge
Starting Net Cash of $2,163M + Cumulative 3Y FCF of $900M - Cumulative Buybacks of $0.00 (reflecting conservative capital allocation while net cash is deployed into loan book growth) - CapEx of $150M = Ending Year 3 Net Cash of $2,913M ($4.90 per share).
1
Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return
With Year 3 Owner Earnings YoY growth projected at 22.0% (g₃ > 15%), we apply a 15.0x P/OE multiple from the Rapid Compounding tier of the Narrow Moat Matrix. Year 3 OE of $1.10 per share × 15.0x ($16.50) + Ending Net Cash of $4.90 per share = $21.40 Expected Fair Value Target, delivering an expected 3-year annualized return (IRR) of 14.4% from today's price of $14.29.
